title: 1hrcm1c
The Incident of the Parchment (Thursday of Calamity) and the Death of the Prophet
hook: The Prophet said, "Let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray." The pen stopped before the right of the Ahl al-Bayt was written.
scenes.0.text: It was the last weeks of the Prophet's life. The Prophet prepared an army to be sent to the area of Belka in the direction of Damascus and brought a young Osama bin Zayed at his head. Usame was very young. His father is Zeyd b. Harise was martyred once before. The army has begun to gather in Jürf, just outside Medina. Some, however, were unwilling to accept such a young man as their commander and openly objected. And so began the first quarrel in the last days of the Prophet's life.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: ulks7y
Usama b. Zayd
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.text: The objections reached the Prophet's ear. At that time, her illness had begun to worsen. And yet he came to the mosque and went to the pulpit. Addressing the protesters, he said that Osama was worthy of command and ordered the army to march. But the tents in the camp in Jurf are still up. The soldiers never left. News of illness from Medina became an excuse to tie up the army. Days passed before the Prophet's order was carried out.
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.text: On one of the worst days of his illness, the Prophet returned to his companions in his room in Medina. "Bring me a pen and paper", he said forcefully. I write you a letter so that you will never go astray after me". This request is being passed on to Buhari and Muslim. The Prophet wanted to leave a last will and testament so that his people would not go astray. He didn't say what he was going to write right away. The Shiites think that this inscription will put on paper the announcement made for **Ali** in Ghadir. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Those who hold fast to the Book and the people of the House will not go astray".
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.text: Before pen and paper could be brought in, there was a quarrel in the room. The sources attribute to Umar the following: "The pain of the disease prevailed over the Prophet. Allah is sufficient for us". Some of the people in the room said to bring what the Prophet wanted. Others supported Umar's words. The voices were getting louder. The Prophet, lying on his sickbed, heard a dispute growing in his head. His last wish was left in the middle of the room's argument. The paper never reached the Prophet's hand.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.4.text: And when the dispute was over, the Prophet said, "Get up and go away from me". It was never written. Years later, **Ibn Abbas** couldn't hold back his tears as he recounted this day. He used to say, "The trouble is that there is noise and discord between the Prophet and that scripture". That's the word Buhari uses. According to the Shiites, the will, which was prevented from being written in that room, paved the way for the right of Hz. Ali to be set aside in Sakife a few days later.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1q0thws
Ibn Abbas
scenes.5.text: The same narration also relates that the Prophet made three oral wills after he could not write. The first was the expulsion of the idolaters from the Arabian Peninsula. The second was that the delegations of the apostles who came to Medina should be received as he himself had received them. The rabbi says he forgot the third will. One of the Prophet's last wills was lost in the memory of the narrator. What's forgotten is not in the narrative. Those who love the Prophet still carry the pain of that missing sentence in their hearts.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.text: The Prophet died in Medina on a Monday in the month of Rabi'ul-awwal, in the eleventh year of the Hijrah. His last moments were led by His Holiness **Ali**. The one who raised his hand at Ghadir witnessed his last breath and closed his blessed eyes. A deep silence fell in the room. It was up to Ali to wash the Prophet's body and bury it. The rest of Medina was still unaware of what had happened.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.7.text: When the news of his death came, there was a great commotion in Medina. Umar didn't accept the Prophet's death at first. Abu Bakr came and announced to the people that the Prophet had died. **Ali** and Hashimov did not leave the funeral. It was their duty to wash the Prophet's body and prepare for burial. On one side of the city, people were crying, while on the other side, a group was heading towards Sakife. And before the body of the prophet was laid in the earth, there was a dispute concerning the kingdom.
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.7.art.actors.2.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.7.art.actors.3.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: The Prophet wishes to have a document written; the saying "pain has overcome him, the Book of God is enough for us", the noise, and Ibn Abbas's "calamity" sentence.
sunni.1.says: The report of the same event; Ibn Abbas weeps.
sunni.2.says: Three bequests: expel the polytheists, host the delegations; the narrator says he forgot the third.
sunni.3.says: "Come, let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray"; the dispute in the setting and the Prophet saying "Get up".
sunni.4.says: The preparation of Usama's army, the objections, and the dispatch of the army in the time of Abu Bakr. (The citations are relayed from WikiShia; the primary texts were not opened.)
sunni.5.says: The preparation of the army and the objections.
sunni.6.says: At the Prophet's death, Umar not accepting the death at first and Abu Bakr announcing the situation.
shia.0.says: A Shia treatise in which the matter of Usama's army is treated from the standpoint of kalam. For the opposing interpretation, Jahiz, al-Uthmaniyya pp. 146-147 is mentioned.
shia.1.says: The story of the Prophet cursing those who do not join the army is told in Shia sources; it is not confirmed by a valid Sunni chain.
disputes.0.title: 10zjtqb
What was to be written?
disputes.0.sunni: There is no report stating the content of the document; because of the dispute, the document was not written. In the Sunni reading, Umar wished not to tire the sick Prophet and recalled the sufficiency of the Qur'an.
disputes.0.shia: There is no report stating the content of the document; because of the dispute, the document was not written. In the Shia reading, this request is understood as a farewell recalling Imam Ali's standing; this is an inference.
disputes.1.title: 1skgrcg
Usama's army
disputes.1.sunni: The Prophet made the young Usama commander; objections arose, and the movement was delayed. In the Sunni reading, this is a preparation made after Mu'ta, and Abu Bakr later sent the army out.
disputes.1.shia: The Prophet appointed young Osama as commander; there was opposition, the move was delayed. In Shia reading, the army is mentioned taking the leading Sahabah out of Medina; the curse narrative is mentioned in sources such as Shahristani and Ibn Abi'l-Hadid; it is not confirmed by a valid Sunni chain.
questions.0: The Prophet went out to the mosque even when his illness was severe and ordered the army to leave, but the army remained in Jurf. Why do you think the Prophet asked for a scripture in the days to come that says, "Do not stray"?
questions.1: Ibn Abbas used to say, "The greatest misfortune is that noise and discord come between the Messenger of Allah and that scripture". Why do you think Ibn Abbas saw the real problem not in the absence of writing, but in the interruption of the debate?
questions.2: The sources have a saying attributed to Umar: "The Book of Allah is sufficient for us". How do you think this relates to the Prophet entrusting the Book and the Ahl al-Bayt together in Ghadir?
questions.3: According to the Shiites, the will, which was prevented from being written in that room, paved the way for Ali's right to be set aside in Sakife a few days later. Why do you think the inability to write made it easier?
summary: Bukhari and Muslim report that the Prophet said, "Let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray," and that the document was not written because of the dispute in the room (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 114; Muslim, Sahih, no. 1637a). In the Shia reading, this farewell request is remembered with love for the Ahl al-Bayt and for Imam Ali's standing.
key: The last testament the Prophet wanted written
notes.0: Before his death the Prophet said «let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray» (Bukhari, Muslim).
notes.1: A dispute broke out in the room and the document was not written.
notes.2: Ibn Abbas would call this day «the real calamity».
notes.3: The Prophet died on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH.
notes.4: This is read as a testament wanting to have Imam Ali's standing written.
